title: FAMILY PLANNING
mv: Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
mvp: “Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” Psalm 127:3
assignment: List five (5) potential dangers or wrong attitudes Christians should avoid when considering family planning (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), “Family planning allows individuals and couples to anticipate and attain their desired number of children as well as the spacing and timing of their births.’’ The Bible does not specifically mention family planning, but according to Luke 14:28-30, Jesus Christ talks about the wisdom behind planning before major decisions are made. It is important to examine God’s plan for the “Family” institution and to understand the reasons for us to plan our families.
The biblical view on family planning can be traced to the importance that God places on fruitfulness and childbearing. These include the fact that:

i: God commands that we should be fruitful and multiply (Genesis 1:28).
Children are one's pride and joy (Psalm 127:5; Proverbs 27:11).
God cherishes children as tools for propagating His Kingdom (Mark 10:14-15).

b.x: However, God’s plan of fruitfulness and multiplication does not call for the neglect of any child in this world (Jeremiah 29:11; Isaiah 65:23).

God gave the human race the grace for increase and procreation. However, wisdom demands that we consider the need to cater for the children God gives, which must include provision of food, shelter, education, etc (1 Timothy 5:8). The reasons for birth control may differ from one family to another. These include:

i: Pleasure: This may be to give room for marital/sexual intimacy (1 Corinthians 7:3-5).
Health, especially of the mother: If and when the life of the wife is at risk, birth control should be considered by the husband as proof of his love (Ephesians 5:28-29).
Resources: Adequate provision is needed for every child. Do not give birth to the children you cannot cater for (1 Timothy 5:8).
Priorities and Necessities: This is to meet other pressing needs such as shelter, career, education, finance, etc (Luke 14:28).
Government Policy: To regulate their population, nations can come up with policies on the acceptable number of children for each family.

b.x: Family planning methods available include the traditional methods, such as abstinence, withdrawal, breastfeeding (amenorrhea), etc. and modern methods like oral contraceptives, injectables, implants, IUDs, barrier (Condoms), and permanent sterilisation options, which include vasectomy for men and tubal ligation for women.
If believers in the Christian family have reasons for family planning, they should consult with the appropriate professionals in that field for proper counselling and recommendations.
Wisdom demands that the number of children given birth to can be adequately catered for (Proverbs 4:7; Ecclesiastes 10:10b).

i: Define family planning according to the W.H.O.
Highlight five biblical views on family planning.
